title: Nintendo Let Philips Make 3 Zelda Games, Then Erased Them
hook:
In 1991 Nintendo dumped Sony for Philips the day after Sony announced their SNES CD deal, and Philips walked away with a license to put Zelda on its CD-i console. Two of those games were made in about a year on roughly 600,000 dollars each, and Nintendo later left them out of its own history book. Which Zelda game would you erase from history?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Nintendo once let another company make three Zelda games, then left them out of its official history books? In nineteen ninety one, Nintendo and Sony were building a CD add-on for the Super Nintendo. Sony announced the partnership at a trade show in Chicago. The very next day, Nintendo held a surprise press conference and said it was working with Philips instead. Philips got a license to put Nintendo characters on its own CD-i console. A small studio called Animation Magic made two Zelda games in just over a year, using animators in Russia. The developer later recalled that each of those games cost roughly six hundred thousand dollars to make. Nintendo only approved the design documents and character sketches. Link: The Faces of Evil and Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon both released in October nineteen ninety three. Wand of Gamelon holds a Guinness World Record as the first Zelda game where you play as Zelda herself. The CD-i itself sold for about seven hundred dollars, and the whole project reportedly lost Philips close to a billion dollars. Years later, the games' cartoon cutscenes became internet memes. Nintendo left them out of the Hyrule Historia book, and Eiji Aonuma said they don't really fit the franchise. Which Zelda game would you erase from history? Follow for more gaming history.
